interface.description: Network interface to capture packets from. Use 'any' for all interfaces.

filter.description: Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) expression to selectively capture packets. Leave empty to capture all.

max_packets.description: Maximum number of packets to capture. 0 means continue until interrupted.

output_mode.description: Format of the output. 'text' = decoded headers, 'hex' = raw hex dump, 'combined' = both.

verbose_data.description: If true, include full packet payload (as hex) in output even in text mode.

snaplen.description: Maximum number of bytes to capture per packet. 0 means capture full packet length.

timestamp_format.description: Format of packet timestamps: 'full' = ISO 8601, 'compact' = Unix epoch, 'relative' = ms since first packet.

include_link_layer.description: Include Ethernet header (e.g., MAC addresses) in decoded output.

rotate_size_mb.description: Maximum size (in MB) of the output file before rotation. 0 disables rotation.

rotate_count.description: Number of rotated files to retain. Used only when rotate_size_mb > 0.

output_file.description: Path to write captured output. Empty string means standard output (console).

daemonize.description: Run ipgrab in the background as a daemon service.

pid_file.description: Path to the PID file when daemonized.

extra_interfaces.description: Additional interfaces to capture on (used when multi-interface mode is desired).

use_buffering.description: Enable internal packet buffering to reduce CPU usage on high-throughput links.

buffer_size.description: Maximum number of packets buffered before flush.

buffer_timeout_ms.description: Maximum time (ms) to wait before flushing buffer, even if not full.

use_priority_filter.description: If supported by the system, filter by packet priority (e.g., from netem or tc).

min_priority.description: Minimum packet priority to capture (0 = highest).
